question: If sin A + cos A = √2 sin A, then what is the value of tanA?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

⇒ sin A + cos A = √2 sin A

⇒ cos A = sin A(√2 − 1) ⇒ cot A = √2 − 1

⇒ tan A = 1 ÷ cot A = 1 ÷ (√2 − 1)

⇒ Rationalizing the denominator gives tan A = √2 + 1

**∴ The correct answer is √2 + 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

sin A + cos A = √2 sin A

**Formula Used:**

tan A = sin A ÷ cos A

(a − b)(a + b) = a² − b²

**Calculations:**

⇒ Divide the entire given equation by cos A:

⇒ (sin A ÷ cos A) + (cos A ÷ cos A) = √2(sin A ÷ cos A)

⇒ tan A + 1 = √2 tan A

⇒ 1 = √2 tan A − tan A

⇒ 1 = tan A(√2 − 1)

⇒ tan A = 1 ÷ (√2 − 1)

⇒ Multiply numerator and denominator by (√2 + 1):

⇒ tan A = (√2 + 1) ÷ [(√2 − 1)(√2 + 1)]

⇒ tan A = (√2 + 1) ÷ [(√2)² − (1)²]

⇒ tan A = (√2 + 1) ÷ (2 − 1)

⇒ tan A = √2 + 1

**∴ The correct answer is √2 + 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Basic Trigonometric Ratios

tan A = sin A ÷ cos A and cot A = cos A ÷ sin A.

Pythagorean Identities

sin² A + cos² A = 1 | 1 + tan² A = sec² A | 1 + cot² A = cosec² A.

Algebraic Rationalization

To rationalize a denominator of the form (a − b), multiply numerator and denominator by its conjugate (a + b) using the identity (a − b)(a + b) = a² − b².
